title: Indian Democracy — Challenges and Responses
shortDescription: Communalism, corruption, criminalisation, inequality and institutional responses.
genZNote: Every democracy has bugs. India's strength is the patches — RTI, Lokpal, ECI rules and PIL.

sections.heading: Challenges
bullets: Communalism, casteism, regionalism and identity conflicts; poverty, inequality and illiteracy.
Corruption, criminalisation of politics and the role of money in elections; defections and weak internal party democracy.
Insurgency and extremism; gender inequality; misinformation and polarisation in media.
Capacity gaps in institutions and pendency of cases.

table.caption: Reform tools
rows: Anti-corruption ombudsman; Lokpal began functioning in 2019
Affidavits of criminal antecedents (ADR, 2002), NOTA, VVPAT, Model Code

sections.heading: Role of Citizens and Civil Society
sections.body: Free media, social movements, voter participation, social audits and civic education strengthen democracy; the Constitution's Fundamental Duties emphasise responsible citizenship.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Indian democracy faces social, political and institutional challenges that are met through legal reforms, judicial review, transparency laws and citizen participation.
keyFacts: RTI 2005; Lokpal Act 2013; Whistle Blowers Act 2014.

commonTraps: Do not say RTI is a fundamental right by name — it flows from Art. 19(1)(a).

sources.name: NCERT, Indian Constitution at Work (Class XI Political Science)
Constitution of India (official text), Legislative Department
